newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares get dollar help to new lifetime high.
newsitem.headline: German shares get dollar help to new lifetime high.

text.p: Germany's blue-chip DAX index climbed over three quarters of a percent to break the key 3,700 level on Friday and remained buoyant to end bourse trade with moderate gains.
The 30-share DAX index ended the session up 22.26 points at 3,695.29 points after hitting a new lifetime high at 3,708.25 and falling on profit-taking ahead of the weekend.
Traders looked for the market to remain strong due to the firmer dollar and to also take its cue in the afternoon from Wall Street and the impact of U.S. May unemployment data due at 1230 GMT.

Among the day's most notable movers was carbon and graphite group SGL Carbon which ended down 21.20 marks at 239 marks on news that authorities in Europe and the United States were investigating the group for allegations of price fixing.
SGL Carbon, which had become a clear market favourite since its bourse listing two years ago, said it would participate in the investigation.
Among other shares, chemical stocks including Hoechst AG, Bayer AG and BASF AG all traded higher, enjoying the prospect of a firmer dollar which makes their exports cheaper abroad.
Deutsche Telekom shares ended up 1.00 marks at 40.15 marks, gaining on follow-through support from a buy recommendation from U.S. securities house Salomon Brothers.
